status: Explicit admission restatement for existing proofs. The smoothness theorem has an earlier pre-proof contract; the present seven-interface statement is not a retrospective pre-proof seal.
objects: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space with its Borel measurable structure; gamma_E is the centered identity-covariance Gaussian probability. H_j is the unnormalized probabilists Hermite polynomial, with Gaussian squared norm j!. L2 means the actual real square-integrable equivalence-class Hilbert space.

interfaces.statement: For every finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space E with its Borel structure and every real polynomial p, each literal ridge x -> p(<w,x>) belongs to L2(gamma_E). There exists a family h(w) of those membership proofs such that w -> (h(w)).toLp of that literal function is globally C-infinity on all of E into L2(gamma_E). No unit-vector, degree, coefficient or derivative bound is assumed.

For every natural degree j and ambient vector w, take the L2 class of the literal probabilists Hermite polynomial H_j(<w,x>) under gamma_E. The definition uses the proved polynomial ridge membership witness and the real coefficient image of the integer Hermite polynomial. This is an actual equivalence class, not an arbitrary feature with assumed Gram identity.

For every finite set S of natural degrees, real coefficient function c, and ambient vector w, define the finite L2 sum F_(S,c)(w)=sum_(j in S)c(j) h_j(w), where h_j is the preceding actual Hermite class. Empty S, degree zero and arbitrary signed or zero coefficients are allowed.

For every natural j the actual Hermite class map h_j:E->L2(gamma_E) is globally C2 on all of E, obtained by specializing polynomial ridge smoothness and lowering the differentiability order. There is no unit-direction premise.

For every natural j and every ambient w, the representative of h_j(w) equals x->H_j(<w,x>) almost everywhere under gamma_E. This is equality of representatives almost everywhere, not pointwise equality at every x.

For every finite S, arbitrary real c, and unit vectors w,z in E, <F_(S,c)(w),F_(S,c)(z)>_(L2(gamma_E))=sum_(j in S)j! c(j)^2 <w,z>^j. The correlation may be negative or equal to either endpoint; degree zero and empty S are included. Both directions must be unit; no independence is assumed.

For every finite S and arbitrary real coefficient function c, F_(S,c):E->L2(gamma_E) is globally C2, as a finite sum of constant scalar multiples of the degreewise smooth maps. There is no unit-direction or summability premise.

proof_topology.text: For each finite exponent q>=1, linear Gaussian projections form a continuous linear Lq-valued map. Prove smoothness of the nth power simultaneously in every finite q, using continuous Holder multiplication L^(2q) times L^(2q) into Lq for the successor.
Polynomial addition and scalar multiplication assemble the smooth L2 map. Almost-everywhere representatives establish literal membership and identify this map with the displayed toLp map.
Specialize to the real image of the integer Hermite polynomial. The toLp representative theorem gives the almost-everywhere identity; lower C-infinity to C2.

Expand the finite L2 inner product bilinearly. The existing exact mixed Gaussian Hermite product identity annihilates unequal degrees and gives j! <w,z>^j on the diagonal. No new orthogonality proof is introduced.
Finite addition of constant scalar multiples preserves global C2.

boundaries: No infinite-Hermite convergence or derivative limit is proved here.
No identification of different feature Hilbert carriers is asserted.
No ambient Gram formula away from unit directions follows from the unit-direction Gram identity.
